cleanIntro: Auto-Ordnance's 1911 book names this gun on its nomenclature page as 'Model: 1911BKO (1911A1)' — the GI-pattern pistol with a spring plug, a barrel bushing and no full-length guide rod. That matters at the front end of the strip, because the plug and the recoil spring are under real compression and the bushing has to be rotated to release them. Wear eye protection: Auto-Ordnance says so at the head of the procedure and it is the plug they are thinking of. Note also that step 8 carries an extra instruction for 1911TCA models about taking the recoil spring out of the front of the slide first — that is not your pistol.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber empty, eye protection on
steps.action: Drop the magazine and clear the chamber before anything else, then put safety glasses on. Auto-Ordnance's warning is specific about why — you are about to release a compressed recoil spring and its plug, and if either gets away from you it goes toward your face. The pistol should be cleaned after every use and any time it has seen dirt or sand.
steps.prose: Condition One in this book means magazine empty and chamber empty. That is the state you want for cleaning.
steps.quote:
WARNING: MAKE SURE YOUR HANDGUN IS UNLOADED BEFORE STARTING THIS PROCEDURE.
WEAR SAFETY GLASSES IN CASE YOU LOSE CONTROL OF A SPRING LOADED COMPONENT SUCH AS THE RECOIL SPRING OR PLUG WHICH COULD INJURE YOUR EYES.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.13
steps.warn: Eye protection is not optional on a GI-pattern 1911 strip.

steps.title: Muzzle up, butt on the bench
steps.action: Stand the pistol on the heel of the butt and the grip safety on a table with the muzzle pointing upward. That grip is what lets you hold the recoil spring plug down with one thumb while the other hand turns the bushing, and it means that if the plug does escape it goes up rather than across the room.
steps.prose: Trying this one-handed in mid-air is how plugs end up in the carpet.
steps.quote: 2. With the muzzle pointing upward, rest the pistol on heel of butt and the grip safety on a table or bench.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.13

steps.title: Plug down, bushing a quarter turn clockwise
steps.action: Push the slide back about a quarter of an inch, press down on the recoil spring plug just below the muzzle, and at the same time rotate the barrel bushing about a quarter turn CLOCKWISE — a bushing wrench if it is tight. That frees the plug and spring. Keep pressure on the plug the whole time and let it extend out gradually; releasing it is the classic 1911 mistake.
steps.prose: The quarter-inch of slide travel is what lines the bushing lug up with its cut. Without it the bushing will not turn.
steps.quote: 3. Push the slide back about 1/4 inch, press down on recoil spring plug (located just below the muzzle) and at the same time rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about 1/4 turn, using a barrel bushing wrench if necessary; this will free the plug and recoil spring. Keep pressure on the plug to prevent it from being ejected by the spring.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.13
steps.warn: Keep a thumb on the plug until the spring is fully extended.

steps.title: Hammer cocked, slide stop out at the disassembly notch
steps.action: Cock the hammer by pulling back on the spur — the slide stop will not clear a down hammer. Then draw the slide back until the lug on the slide stop lines up with the disassembly notch in the slide, push inward on the end of the slide stop shaft from the RIGHT side, and pull the slide stop out from the LEFT.
steps.prose: The notch is the small semicircular cut ahead of the slide stop notch. Line it up before you push, not while.
steps.caution: Do not lever the slide stop out with a screwdriver — that is what puts the idiot scratch on a 1911 frame.
steps.quote: 6. Pull slide to rear until lug on slide stop is opposite disassembly notch (see picture #6) and push inward on the end of the slide stop shaft on the right side of the pistol and remove the slide stop from the left side.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.13

steps.title: Slide forward, spring and guide out to the rear
steps.action: Run the slide forward off the front of the frame. Turn it upside down, lift the recoil spring and guide and pull them REARWARD out of the slide. If you had a 1911TCA model the spring might have to come out of the front first — but this is not that pistol, and on a GI-pattern gun the guide comes out the back.
steps.prose: Do not let the hammer fall while the slide is off the frame. Auto-Ordnance calls that out specifically.
steps.quote: 8. Turn the slide upside down and lift the recoil spring and guide and pull them rearward out of the slide (see picture #7). For 1911TCA models, it may be required to remove the recoil spring from the front of the slide before removing the recoil guide rearward.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.14
steps.warn: NOTE: Do not drop the hammer while slide is removed from the frame.

steps.title: Bushing anticlockwise, then barrel out the front
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing ANTICLOCKWISE — the opposite way to the release turn — and push the barrel and bushing forward until the bushing clears the slide, then slip the bushing off the barrel. Finally push the barrel link forward and lift the barrel out of the slide.
steps.prose: The link must be forward or the barrel lugs will not clear their recesses. It swings freely; a nudge with a fingernail is enough.
steps.aside: 10. Push barrel link forward and remove barrel from the slide.
steps.quote: 9. Turn barrel bushing counterclockwise, push barrel and barrel bushing forward until bushing is clear of the slide, then remove bushing from the barrel.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.14

steps.title: Bore wet, then brushed, then dry and examined
steps.action: Run a patch wetted with a good cleaning solution through the bore several times, then a bristle brush wetted the same way back and forth the full length of the bore AND chamber. Follow with dry patches and look down it. Fouling in the bore costs accuracy, and grease accumulating in the chamber is what stops cartridges feeding properly out of the magazine.
steps.prose: The chamber is the part people skip on a 1911 because the barrel is out and it looks clean. It is not.
steps.quote: 2. Using a cleaning rod, run a patch wetted with a high quality gun cleaning solution through the bore several times. Then attach a bristle brush wetted with a high quality gun cleaning solution to the rod and run it back and forth the full length of the bore and chamber. Clean bore with dry patches and examine.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Care and Cleaning of the Pistol, p.18

steps.title: Powder residue off everything, then a very light oil
steps.action: Take the powder residue off every component with solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush. Then run a dry patch through the bore, follow it with a very lightly oiled one, wipe all surfaces clean and finish with a very lightly oiled cloth. Light is the operative word: excess oil collects grit and congeals in the cold, and on a 1911 that means a slide that will not run.
steps.prose: A film you can see is already too much. Auto-Ordnance says only a light application is needed for both lubrication and rust protection.
steps.caution: NOTE: Only a light application of oil is needed to provide adequate lubrication of moving parts and to prevent rust.
steps.quote: 3. Using a high quality cleaning solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush, remove powder residue from all components of the pistol. After cleaning, run a dry patch through the bore, then follow with a patch that is very lightly oiled.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Care and Cleaning of the Pistol, p.18

steps.title: Stop here — and leave the safety parts alone
steps.action: Do not strip the pistol any further than the ten steps above. Auto-Ordnance puts it in capitals and adds a specific prohibition: do not remove or alter parts, particularly SAFETY parts. On a 1911 that means the thumb safety, the grip safety and the firing pin plunger lever, all of which are load-bearing for whether the gun fires when you did not intend it to.
steps.prose: If more maintenance is genuinely needed the manual sends you to its shipping-for-service section, not to a screwdriver.
steps.quote: DO NOT STRIP YOUR PISTOL ANY FURTHER THAN PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED. DO NOT REMOVE OR ALTER PARTS, PARTICULARLY SAFETY PARTS. IF ADDITIONAL MAINTENANCE IS REQUIRED SEE “SHIPPING FIREARMS FOR SERVICE” ON PAGE 19.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Disassembly of the Auto-Ordnance 1911 Models for Routine Cleaning, p.14

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring, recoil spring guide, recoil spring plug and slide stop — the classic seven-piece GI strip. That is exactly the extent Auto-Ordnance describes and exactly where they stop you. Reassembly reverses it, with one thing to watch: the firing pin plunger lever must be down and out of the slide's path before the slide stop goes back in.
steps.prose: The magazine can be stripped separately for cleaning; that is its own section and is not part of the field strip.
steps.quote: 1. Disassemble (field-strip) the handgun to the extent described on page 13.
steps.cite: OWNER’S MANUAL FOR AUTO-ORDNANCE 1911 MODELS — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Care and Cleaning of the Pistol, p.18

deepAbsentReason: Auto-Ordnance publishes NO deeper procedure for this pistol and forbids one in capitals immediately after the last disassembly step: 'DO NOT STRIP YOUR PISTOL ANY FURTHER THAN PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED. DO NOT REMOVE OR ALTER PARTS, PARTICULARLY SAFETY PARTS. IF ADDITIONAL MAINTENANCE IS REQUIRED SEE “SHIPPING FIREARMS FOR SERVICE” ON PAGE 19.' (p.14). The only other teardown in the book is the magazine, which is a separate component and is covered in its own section rather than as a deeper clean of the pistol. There is therefore nothing published to walk, and a 1911 detail strip — firing pin stop, extractor, mainspring housing, sear and disconnector — would be invented against an explicit prohibition.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Wet patches through the bore several times with a quality cleaning solution
Bristle brush, wetted, back and forth the full length of bore AND chamber
Dry patches, then examine the bore
Grease left in the chamber interferes with feeding — get it out

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush to take powder residue off all components
Clean the slide rails, the breech face and around the extractor
Wipe all surfaces clean, then wipe them with a VERY lightly oiled cloth
Do not remove or alter any part, and particularly not a safety part

cleaning.name: BARREL GROUP
tasks: Clean the barrel exterior, the lugs and the link
Clean the inside of the barrel bushing and the muzzle end of the slide it rides in
Wipe the recoil spring, guide and plug and leave them lightly oiled

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wipe the body, follower and feed lips; do not oil the inside
Never use a damaged, non-standard or improperly assembled magazine
Do not spray or apply lubricant directly onto ammunition

reassembly: With the slide upside down and the barrel link forward, put the barrel back into the slide.
Fit the barrel bushing over the barrel and into the slide, then turn it back clockwise to lock it.

Seat the recoil spring on the guide with the closed end against the guide's collar, push the spring through the slide from the rear, and position the arched part of the guide over the barrel just ahead of the link.
Cock the hammer and check the firing pin plunger lever is DOWN and out of the slide's path before the slide goes on.

Run the slide onto the frame, look through the slide stop hole, insert the slide stop almost fully, push the slide back until the disassembly notch lines up, then push the slide stop up and in against its plunger until fully seated.
Fit the recoil spring plug over the spring, press it down and rotate the bushing anticlockwise a quarter turn to capture it.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed somewhere safe, check the slide runs fully forward into battery under its own spring and that the barrel locks up — press the muzzle back and confirm the slide is not standing out of battery. Check the slide stop is fully seated by looking at both sides of the frame. Cock the hammer and confirm the thumb safety engages and holds it, then that the grip safety must be depressed for the trigger to move; both are safety parts the manual forbids altering, so a failure here is a gunsmith job, not an adjustment. Finally cycle an empty magazine to confirm the slide locks back on empty.
